title: Bridge signal & roadmap recalibrate
summary: Leadership all-hands focusing on near-term operational resilience and a short roadmap re-prioritization. Open discussion about the June 2 incident, hiring velocity, and a small scope shift to prioritize reliability/observability work. Clear next steps: run an infra playbook tabletop, slow roll a reliability-focused sprint, update the public roadmap, and align hires to runway constraints.
next_steps: Diego to schedule incident tabletop by 2027-06-22
Ravi and Aisha to draft a 6-week reliability sprint plan by 2027-06-20
Product to publish an updated Q3 roadmap snapshot on 2027-06-18
People Ops to pause external hiring for non-critical IC roles until reforecast complete (update by 2027-06-21)
Maya to share updated OKR adjustments and a short note to company by 2027-06-16
action_items: Diego: run post-mortem doc + tabletop invite; due 2027-06-22
Ravi: propose reliability sprint scope + team allocations; due 2027-06-20
Aisha: cost/latency tradeoff memo for batch caching changes; due 2027-06-24
Maya: update public roadmap and company note; due 2027-06-16
Olivia: short-term hiring freeze checklist + exceptions; due 2027-06-21
header: Date: 2027-06-15 10:00 PDT | Duration: 1:04 | Location: All-hands (Hybrid) | Recording: enabled | Attendees: leadership + engineering squads
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining a little bit earlier today. We wanted to use this slot to surface the June ops stuff and talk about what we reprioritize for Q3. Welcome, and if you are remote just drop questions in chat.
[00:22] Ethan Kaplan: Quick note, high level — great work closing a lot of feature tickets Q2, but the June 2nd incident was a reminder: customers noticed tail latency and a few hosted routing fallbacks. We need a short, intense focus on reliability and observability.
[00:38] Lena Ortiz: Can you remind folks of the impact? I saw the dashboard spike but want the concrete customer impact for context.
[00:46] Diego Morales: Sure — from the post-incident logs: we had a routing cascade after an autoscaler mis-reconciliation. Latency p50 stayed fine, p95 jumped to ~2.4s for text-gen, p99 to 6s for a small subset, and a handful of requests hit fallback models in the wrong region. There were customer errors flagged, two dedicated customers opened support tickets. Our rollback recovered traffic in 18 minutes but the customer experience was impacted.
[01:20] Marcus Lee: There's also some noise from the KV cache eviction pattern — I think it exacerbated the regen of KV state. The transcript here is approximating the technical — but the core issue was autoscale + cache thrash.
[01:37] Ravi Sundaram: Yeah and we found an edge case in the autoscaler control loop where a race condition plus metric lag led to overprovisioning then sudden instance churn. We're already shipping a guard to smooth that control loop, but we probably need a canary and a tabletop to validate.
[01:57] Maya Chen: OK, so immediate question to leadership: do we pause any new non-critical launches for the next three weeks? We need to redirect some engineering cycles to reliability.
[02:08] Aisha Patel: I think yes, at least a soft pause. We should only block launches if there's aligned risk. We have maybe 12 FTE-equivalents we can shift for 6 weeks without killing runway. But we need product to own the scope so we don't go too broad.
[02:28] Priya Nair: To be clear, product supports a targeted reliability sprint — but we need to communicate to customers about increased monitoring and a plan so enterprise accounts don't get surprises.
[02:39] Ethan Kaplan: Right. Maya, can you own the company note? Short and transparent: what happened, how we mitigated, what we're doing next.
[02:49] Maya Chen: Yep, I'll draft the note and post tomorrow.
[02:52] [03:00] Olivia Park: On hiring — People Ops recommends pausing non-critical externally posted roles until we reforecast, but continuing with critical roles (SRE, core serving runtime eng). We also have a small backlog of offers to finalize — do we proceed?
[03:16] Ethan Kaplan: I want to be conservative: final offers for roles committed to customer SLOs yes; everything else, pause. Keep current candidate pipelines warm but don't extend offers until we have a short-window reforecast.
[03:29] Samir Gupta: On cost — if we prioritize reliability we may take a slight hit to unit costs initially due to reduced batching, more conservative autoscaling, and extra shadowing. We need to estimate the delta and bake into the reforecast.
[03:46] Aisha Patel: Agreed. Ravi, can we get an estimate of token-cost impact if we increase per-request isolation and reduce cross-tenant batching for two weeks?
[03:56] Ravi Sundaram: Rough quick numbers — ballpark 10-18% increase in token cost for the most affected routes if we isolate, but we can mitigate with KV prefix caching and selective batching for low-latency routes. We'll put a narrower set of experiments together.
[04:14] [04:30] Diego Morales: I also want to highlight observability gaps. We need better end-to-end tracing so when a region fallback happens we can see the decision path — route policy, model variant, autoscale signals. That will help shorten MTTR.
[04:43] Marcus Lee: There's a lack of a single source of truth for per-request routing decisions — logs live in multiple systems. We should consolidate a small routing-trace pipeline.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Good. So proposal: 6-week reliability sprint, focused workstreams: autoscaler hardening, KV cache stability, routing-trace consolidation, customer-facing monitoring. Keep feature work to a minimum and only critical launches.
[05:12] Priya Nair: For the sprint, what's the acceptance criteria? Reduced p99 by what percent? Fewer fallback incidents?
[05:20] Aisha Patel: We should aim for p99 reduction of 30% on affected routes and zero unplanned region fallbacks in the sprint window. Also reduce incident-to-detect time by 50% via improved signals.
[05:34] Ethan Kaplan: And OKRs will reflect that — we can temporarily shift 1-2 OKRs to be reliability-first.
[05:40] [06:00] Maya Chen: Hiring alignment: SRE and runtime team hires continue. Everything else paused. Olivia, you'll finalize a short exceptions doc?
[06:08] Olivia Park: Yes, will do and share by Monday.
[06:12] Samir Gupta: Customers — do we proactively reach out to the two impacted customers with a dedicated runbook and offer to run a landing page with their routing bleed?
[06:22] Priya Nair: We should. Customer success will own outreach and offer a technical review session.
[06:27] Ethan Kaplan: Good. Also I want to surface the budget conversation — series C runway metrics look fine but this reliability focus will consume some reserved capacity and maybe increase short-term spend. Finance and product should do a reforecast.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Action: reforecast due by end of next week, and hiring paused until that is done.
[06:44] [07:00] Ravi Sundaram: Quick technical aside — regarding KV cache: we should change eviction policy to be latency-aware, and implement a slow warm-up for large model KV loads. That will reduce thrash.
[07:14] Marcus Lee: There was also a mislabeling of the model variant in a fallback route — transcription here sometimes reads 'redwood-lite' but internal labels differ; we should reconcile naming so logs match the model catalog.
[07:28] Maya Chen: Good catch. Clean naming for models in logs and the model catalog — Diego, add that to the PM/infra checklist.
[07:36] Diego Morales: Will do.
[07:38] [08:00] Audience Q&A (mixed remote/chat):
[08:05] Question (Engineer in chat): How long is the pause for feature launches?
[08:09] Maya Chen: Initial plan is 6 weeks, with weekly reviews. We will open exceptions for time-sensitive launches (customer SLA commitments, security fixes).
[08:18] Question (Lead PM): Will this affect Dedicated and Private deployment offerings?
[08:22] Aisha Patel: We will treat Dedicated customer SLAs as highest priority and keep those flows isolated from the feature pause; Private deployments with air-gapped on-prem are unaffected as they have their own stack.
[08:34] Question (Finance): Will increased spend be covered from reforecast or do we stage cuts?
[08:39] Ethan Kaplan: Use reforecast first, but if the delta is material we'll propose a short reallocation of experiments budget.
[08:46] [09:00] Maya Chen: Ok, quick recap — Diego to run the incident tabletop by next Tuesday; Ravi + Aisha to propose a focused 6-week sprint; Maya publishes a note tomorrow; People Ops pauses non-critical hiring and publishes exceptions; Product publishes a trimmed Q3 roadmap snapshot Friday. Any blockers?
[09:22] Priya Nair: Need support from data on how many customers were impacted by fallback and which routes — I'll follow up with Samir after the call.
[09:30] Samir Gupta: I'll share the route impact spreadsheet by EOD.
[09:34] Diego Morales: Also will attach the short post-mortem doc to the meeting notes.
[09:38] Ethan Kaplan: Thanks team. This is the right short-term move — protect reliability, be honest with customers, and get back to growth.
[09:48] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll close us out and post the notes.
[09:52] [10:00] Meeting ended

Notes: deck posted: https://internal.redwood/platform-q2-ops-deck (internal). Post-incident spreadsheet and draft post-mortem attached to the meeting invite. There was light crosstalk and a few transcription errors (model names, acronyms).
